thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: P0 - node heartbeat missing (gpu-host-77). autodetect: kubelet_unready, last_seen: 2026-03-14T03:30:00Z
pagerduty: Pager P0 triggered for team: eng-oncall - incident: pgd_48622 - escalations enabled
maya: acked. picking this up. I see kubelet not ready from prometheus alert, node stopped answering health probes.
aj: oncall here. maya — any idea if this is a single host or whole rack?
maya: looks isolated to gpu-host-77. adjacency graph shows other hosts in the AZ healthy.
sara: saw a kernel oops log earlier in the logs aggregator for that host at ~03:28 UTC, repeated GPU driver messages. linking logs: https://logs.redwood.example/host/gpu-host-77/2026-03-14
aj: can someone check console? serial console attach request sent to ipmi-runner.
devops-bot: serial-console: request accepted, session id sc-8891. attaching...
maya: attached. console shows kernel panic stack and then machine reboot loop. kernel msg: "[  123.456] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at ffffffff0000"
sara: NVMe errors before the panic too: "nvme0: I/O 0x... timeout". might be unrelated but noted.
aj: customer impact? any active jobs on that node?
maya: two Dedicated pools had running jobs: customer-cpu-bound-1 (no GPUs) had pods evicted earlier. GPU workloads: batch-infer-3 lost 2 replicas. Looks like requests in-flight failed ~03:29.
sara: checking console for graceful shutdown — none. kubelet died. controller-manager detected node NotReady at 03:30:14 and started eviction timers.
aj: start mitigation: cordon + drain? we should avoid draining if node is in reboot loop and pods will be recreated elsewhere, but do cordon first.
maya: cordoning now: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-77` -> success.
devops-bot: cordon recorded by runbook-audit.
aj: initiating drain for GPU pods only (to avoid long eviction for bulk stateful sets). `kubectl drain gpu-host-77 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='component in (gpu-worker,batch-infer)' --force`
maya: drain in progress. some pods stuck terminating (nvidia-driver-plugin). I will force-delete remaining stuck pods after 30s.
sara: meanwhile reroute traffic for live customers: Failover policy applied to route requests off the Dedicated pool in az-1 to az-2. Console shows 95% of traffic moved within 40s.
aj: good. incident-bot: create incident ticket and link to customer impact page.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-77 - Node failure gpu-host-77. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0314-77
maya: alerting support for affected customers: created support tickets for accounts running batch-infer-3 and chocolate-ml-prod.
sara: any signs this is a hardware trigger or driver regression? kernel panic stackpoints to nvidia module but also NVMe errors. opening a hardware ticket with colo ops.
aj: escalate to L2 infra: @sara @kevin please join if available.
sara: pinged kevin in infra channel. he acknowledged and is booting the host into rescue mode for disk checks.
maya: force-deleted 3 stuck pods. drain completed. pods recreated on other nodes successfully.
aj: customer impact update: 2 customers experienced transient failures for ~90s, retries succeeded for most jobs. sent preliminary status to CS.
sara: continuing investigation — capturing dmesg, kernel stack and panic logs. saving a copy to S3: s3://incidents/2026-03-14/gpu-host-77/
maya: plan: 1) keep node cordoned, 2) hardware diag, 3) if hardware ok, repro test with same driver version in staging; 4) rollout mitigation (driver lock or kernel patch) if needed.
aj: oncall handoff: i'll remain until 04:30 UTC. Maya, if you need me after that please escalate to next oncall.
maya: noted. I'll triage postmortem template and start timeline.
incident-bot: scheduled follow-up: postmortem draft requested - due 2026-03-18.
sara: summary for status page: "Partial service interruption for batch inference in az-1 between 03:29 and 03:31 UTC due to a single host kernel panic. Failover completed automatically; impact limited to queued jobs. No customer data lost."
aj: thanks team. closing pager. pagerduty: Pager P0 resolved by maya at 03:36 UTC.
pagerduty: Incident pgd_48622 acknowledged and closed.
maya: adding remediation tasks to backlog and will attach logs.
(emoji) :thumbsup: from kevin in infra channel.
